newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - GDP, Chicago Purchasers.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - GDP, Chicago Purchasers.

text.p: U.S. debt markets appear prepared to tolerate a report on speedy first-quarter economic growth, and may find encouragement in three monthly manufacturing surveys due Wednesday, economists said.

The Commerce Department publishes its advance estimate of first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) on Wednesday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists in a Reuters poll projected a 4.1-percent annual growth rate for the period, up from 3.8 percent in fourth-quarter 1996.
"The focus is GDP. If it's as expected, the market will probably continue to have a positive tone," said Michelle Colley Laughlin, money market economist at Prudential Securities Inc.
Even a reading a couple of tenths higher might be taken in stride by market players, depending on the source of the report's strength, analysts said.
Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Markets, said consumption figures would be carefully scrutinized.
"If for whatever reason consumer spending is less than expected, or business fixed investment is less than expected, that might give the market another lift," Low said.
In recent speeches, Federal Reserve officials underscored their concern that economic friction may erupt from strong consumer demand.

Other components of the report may not have as much market impact. Disagreement about how greatly the international trade deficit weighed on GDP, for instance, has made it less of a focus, analysts said.
"If it turns out the trade deficit was worse than we expected, that's not going to have a big impact on the market," Low said.

In other facets of the GDP release, the chain-weighted price index was forecast up 2.1 percent against 1.9 percent in the last report, and the implicit deflator was expected to read 1.7 percent compared with 1.5 percent.
Monthly indices of national and regional manufacturing activity also await market attention Wednesday morning.

The Chicago purchasing managers survey, set for release at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, stands chief among them. It is widely regarded as the best indicator of the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) nationwide index, to be published Thursday.
Economists forecast Chicago PMI would read 56.2 in April, just below its March reading of 57.5.
Similar results were expected from surveys published at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT by the American Production & Inventory Control Society (APICS) and at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT by the New York branch of NAPM.

"Most manufacturing-sector indicators have weakened up a bit, probably due to the strikes at various automotive plants," Laughlin said. "There's probably a better chance those (indices) are favorable for the market."

A slew of Fed governors and regional bank presidents speak Wednesday at a Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago conference on banking. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan speaks there Thursday at 0925 EDT/1325 GMT.
Separately, Jack Guynn, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, addresses New Orleans Rotary members at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT.
"The market's obviously going to try to gauge the Fed's reaction to (Tuesday's) positive numbers," Laughlin said.
